title: offload-to-external.sh deletes originals after a verification that is blind to the metadata it just destroyed
description:
VERIFIED 2026-08-17.

scripts/offload-to-external.sh:136  rsync -a --info=stats2 "$src"/ "$dst"/
scripts/offload-to-external.sh:139  diff="$(rsync -an --delete --itemize-changes "$src"/ "$dst"/)"
scripts/offload-to-external.sh:146  rm -rf -- "$src"

Two independent defects compound into permanent data loss:

1. COPY DROPS METADATA. 'rsync -a' carries no xattrs, no ACLs, no resource forks —
   measured on BOTH /usr/bin/rsync (openrsync) and rsync 3.4.1. Fidelity needs
   -aHAX --fileflags (see nato-b6h.7 for the full matrix).

2. VERIFICATION CANNOT SEE THAT. Reproduced: source file with xattr user.probe,
   destination without it, identical size and mtime. 'rsync -an --delete
   --itemize-changes' prints NOTHING, so $diff is empty, so the script reports
   'verified' and proceeds to rm -rf the source. The proof is blind to exactly the
   loss the copy caused, because it is also missing -AX.

The script's own help calls the kaspad target 'real data, not a cache'.

3. Also: openrsync rejects --info=stats2 outright ('unrecognized option'), so on a
   stock Mac with no homebrew rsync the copy step fails. That path at least fails
   safe — the || guard returns 1 before the rm — but the script is simply
   non-functional there, and it invokes bare 'rsync' from PATH so which binary it
   gets is whatever the machine happens to have.

Fix direction: copy with ditto --rsrc --extattr --acl, or with an rsync proven to
accept -AX --fileflags; and make the verification compare the metadata it claims to
have preserved, not just size and mtime.
close_reason: Fixed in e97de2c: copy with ditto --rsrc --extattr --acl, verify with a manifest that compares structure, sizes, xattr names, ACLs and symlink targets. Proven both ways — an honest copy round-trips all metadata and removes the source; the old lossy copier shadowed back in is now caught, reported, and the source left intact.

title: rgigasync run as documented silently destroys every piece of macOS metadata
description:
VERIFIED 2026-08-17 on macOS 15.5 with rsync 3.4.1 on PATH. Source file carried 3 xattrs (com.apple.ResourceFork, com.apple.metadata:kMDItemWhereFroms, user.rdirstat.probe), one ACL entry, a 19-byte resource fork; source tree also had an empty directory. Running the tool exactly as its Readme documents — rgigasync -- "-av" src/ dst/ — produced a destination with ZERO xattrs, no ACL, no resource fork, and no empty directory. Only the symlink survived. Cause: rsync.rs:8 hardcodes -lptgoD and never passes -AX --fileflags, so metadata is dropped even when the rsync in PATH is fully capable.

Measured fidelity matrix, same fixture:
  ditto --rsrc --extattr --acl              xattrs Y  acl Y  rsrc 19B  emptydir Y  symlink Y
  /usr/bin/rsync -a (openrsync 2.6.9-compat) xattrs N  acl N  rsrc 0    emptydir Y  symlink Y
  rsync 3.4.1 -aHAX --fileflags --crtimes    xattrs Y  acl Y  rsrc 19B  emptydir Y  symlink Y
  rsync 3.4.1 -a                             xattrs N  acl N  rsrc 0    emptydir Y  symlink Y
  rgigasync -- '-av' (as documented)         xattrs N  acl N  rsrc 0    emptydir N  symlink Y

This confirms the recorded prior call in relocate.rs:25-29 (ditto, not rsync) for the SYSTEM rsync, and shows a modern rsync is only metadata-faithful when the caller passes -AX --fileflags, which rgigasync never does.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-08-17, raised by the rgigasync-56 session and independently re-verified here.

My original claim that openrsync lacks --from0 was WRONG. It accepts it:
  printf 'a.txt\0sub/b.txt\0' > l0.txt
  /usr/bin/rsync -lptgoD --from0 --files-from=l0.txt src/ dst/   -> exit 0, 2 files transferred
--from0 is present as the short flag -0, visible in the usage line's
[-0468BCDEFHIKLOPRSTWVabcdghiklnopqrtuvxyz]. I had grepped --help for the literal
string 'from0', got nothing, and reported the grep miss as absence.

What still stands, re-verified:
  /usr/bin/rsync --xattrs --version  -> exit 1
  /usr/bin/rsync --acls   --version  -> exit 1
So openrsync can take a NUL-separated batch list but cannot carry xattrs or ACLs.
The measured fidelity matrix is unaffected; only the --from0 sentence was wrong.

Consequence for the design: batching is NOT the thing the system rsync cannot do.
Fidelity is. That narrows the gap between openrsync and rsync 3.x to exactly the
metadata flags, and it removes one argument for requiring a modern rsync.

title: [bug] Snapshot checksum disagrees between write and read above 8192 nodes
description:
CONFIRMED by nato-rdirstat-38's rust-skills reviewer, reproduced independently in Python. crates/rdirstat-core/src/snapshot.rs (UNTRACKED as of this filing — never committed, so no blame trail).

MECHANISM: Checksum::write folds bytes.len() on every call, before the words. The WRITER feeds each section in 8192-element blocks (nodes, dir ids, dir totals — each sink.put(&block) is one Checksum::write), so it folds N block lengths. The READER hashes each section in ONE call funnelling to checksum.write(&buffer), so it folds one total length. The two therefore compute different digests as soon as a section exceeds one block.

REPRODUCTION (OFFSET 0xcbf29ce484222325, PRIME 0x100000001b3):
  8192 nodes, 1 block  -> writer 0x88d4a2ce0d441377 == reader  MATCH
  8193 nodes, 2 blocks -> writer 0x4b7200868e21f528 != reader 0x7eca6d3a948689ae
  10000 nodes          -> writer 0xfbb5cb5b44361ecd != reader 0xfe2d731a91084ff5
  69000 nodes          -> writer 0x8da5550a98a49405 != reader 0x5a79a299beaf28f9

IMPACT: every snapshot above 8192 nodes fails its own verification with SnapshotError::ChecksumMismatch. That is every real scan; the design profile is 69M nodes. It passes CI only because the sole round-trip test (a_snapshot_round_trips_the_whole_arena) uses a FIVE-node fixture — three orders of magnitude below BLOCK_NODES. FIX THE TEST FIRST: a fixture at 8193 nodes, or a proptest over arbitrary node counts, fails on the first run.

SECOND FINDING, same file, lower severity: snapshot::read stages the whole node section into vec![0u8; length] while the parsed Vec<Node> is also alive, not released until drop(raw_nodes). At the design profile that is ~6.16 GiB for the node array alone against the 5.0 GiB target in docs/01-ARCHITECTURE.md:144-151. The WRITE path already refuses to do this and explains why in a comment ('a snapshot write must not double the process's peak RSS'); the read path has the same problem unmitigated. The same BLOCK_NODES streaming fix applies.

NOT filed by the author of snapshot.rs and not owned by this session — recorded so a confirmed data-correctness bug in an uncommitted file does not evaporate when its author's session ends.
close_reason: Fixed by nato-rdirstat-ee in d3e30bb, the owner of snapshot.rs. Checksum now carries a partial 64-bit word across write() calls and folds the total length once in finish(), so the digest is a pure function of the byte stream regardless of chunking. Regression tests at 8191/8192/8193/24583 nodes (8192 included deliberately — it is a single block and the bug is invisible there) plus a chunking-independence test feeding identical bytes at 11 split points and in 7-byte dribbles. ee also deleted one of their own tests that asserted the opposite property and had encoded the bug. The lower-severity RSS finding is fixed too: read() now streams through take_records() with a one-block staging buffer, so the encoded section and the parsed Vec<Node> are no longer live simultaneously. Filed by nato-rdirstat-58 on behalf of a finding by nato-rdirstat-38's reviewer; recorded because the file was untracked at the time and the finding would have died with its session.

title: A remote destination reopens the transfer-engine call: ditto cannot write to S3
description:
NEW EVIDENCE, 2026-08-17, arriving AFTER council nato-b6h closed. Not yet a reversal, but it
touches the premise the call rested on and should be looked at before the two paths diverge.

A neighbouring session landed 9ad8396 'feat(remote): reach S3, WebDAV and SFTP from one crate',
adding crates/rdirstat-remote — a validated endpoint, a secret bundle, and a planner that decides
what the far side already holds, over OpenDAL.

The council chose ditto --bom (option E) over an rsync-based engine, and a load-bearing reason was
that BOTH SIDES ARE LOCAL BLOCK DEVICES: that is what makes a byte-for-byte compare affordable and
what makes ditto — a local-filesystem copier — the right tool. ditto cannot write to an S3 bucket.
So option E does not extend to a remote destination, and was never claimed to.

Two things to watch, neither yet wrong:

1. A SECOND SYSTEM OF RECORD FOR 'what does the destination already have'. sync.rs::walk answers
   that for a local destination by stat-ing each path; rdirstat-remote's planner answers the same
   question for a remote one. That is the Architecture & Scale council's Record Keeper red line —
   'a second store claims truth for a fact the spine already stores'. It may well be legitimate,
   because the two answer it by genuinely different means (a stat vs an ETag), but the RULE for
   deciding 'missing / differs / present' should live in one place even when the probe differs.

2. It partially vindicates the REJECTED option A — a transfer abstraction — for a reason nobody
   argued at the time. The council rejected A on throughput and on the capability probe being
   self-defeating; every seat's reasoning was about which LOCAL copier is fastest and most
   faithful. Destination heterogeneity was not on the table because rdirstat-remote did not exist
   yet. An abstraction over 'local disk vs object store' is a different proposition from an
   abstraction over 'ditto vs rsync', and the council's reasoning does not dispose of it.

Recorded reversal conditions R1-R4 on the epic do NOT cover this. This is a fifth.

Next step: read crates/rdirstat-remote's planner against sync.rs::walk and decide whether the
missing/differs/present rule is shared or duplicated. Convene only if it is duplicated.

title: Transfer manager: a persistent job queue with progress, pause, resume and cancel
description: Jobs outlive the process. A queue persisted to app data, one bounded worker pool, per-job byte and file progress emitted as throttled events, and pause/resume/cancel that take effect mid-transfer. This is also where nato-6zb's progress+cancel requirement (council condition C4) gets satisfied for remote copies.
acceptance_criteria: A queued job survives an app restart and resumes from where it stopped; cancel takes effect within one chunk and leaves no partial object claimed as complete; progress events are throttled and sequenced like scan events; a failed job records the reason per file rather than aborting the queue.

title: Keychain-backed credential resolution for remote targets
description: S3 resolution order: explicit key in the macOS Keychain, then AWS_* env, then ~/.aws/credentials + SSO, then IAM role. WebDAV passwords come from the Keychain. SFTP uses ssh-agent and ~/.ssh/config and stores nothing. Endpoint definitions go to settings.json; a secret must never reach that file.
acceptance_criteria: A secret written for a target is readable back and is absent from settings.json on disk; deleting a target deletes its Keychain item; an S3 target with no stored key still works when AWS_* env is set.

title: Remote sync planning: decide what the destination is missing without downloading it
description: The local planner stats both sides and can byte-compare. A remote planner cannot: listing is paged and network-bound, and content comparison means either a checksum the backend already holds or a full download. Tiers: Missing (not in the remote listing), SizeDiffers, ContentDiffers (only where the backend offers a usable checksum). There is no statfs on a bucket, so the local NotEnoughSpace preflight does not apply and must not be faked.
acceptance_criteria: A plan against a remote destination reports the same shape as SyncPlan; the free-space field is explicitly absent rather than zero; a backend with no checksum support degrades to size-only comparison and says so in a warning.

title: rdirstat-remote: target model, connection profiles, and the OpenDAL operator
description: New workspace crate. Owns RemoteKind (S3/WebDAV/SFTP), RemoteTarget (the secret-free, persisted endpoint definition), the built-in connection profiles, and construction of an opendal::Operator from a target plus resolved credentials. No tauri dependency, per crates/AGENTS.md.
acceptance_criteria: A RemoteTarget round-trips through serde; an invalid target is rejected with a typed error naming the field; operator construction is unit-tested for all three kinds without network access; probe() reports reachability as data, never a panic.

title: [epic] Remote targets and transfer management: S3, WebDAV, SFTP
description: The sync engine is local-only: sync.rs plans against two local directories and copies with mkbom + ditto --bom (council decision nato-b6h, option E). Remote destinations break every assumption that rests on — no ditto, no statfs free-space check, no ACL/xattr fidelity, no local byte-compare. This epic lands a remote backend layer, a persistent transfer manager, and the UI for both.
design:
DECIDED WITH THE USER, 2026-08-17:

LIBRARY: Apache OpenDAL only. Rejected s3sync (S3-only, cannot serve WebDAV or
SCP; 359 crates for one protocol; declares rust-version 1.94.1 against this
workspace's declared MSRV of 1.90). OpenDAL covers S3 + WebDAV + SFTP behind one
Operator API for 265 crates at MSRV 1.91, Apache-2.0, already inside deny.toml's
allow list. Its SFTP service drives the system ssh via openssh, so SCP inherits
~/.ssh/config, ssh-agent and existing keys and needs no credential vault.

SCOPE: remote as destination, PLUS a persistent transfer manager — a queue that
survives app restart, with per-job progress, pause/resume/cancel. Download and
remote->remote are follow-ups.

CREDENTIALS: S3 resolves in order — explicit key in the macOS Keychain, AWS_*
env, ~/.aws/credentials + SSO, IAM role — so the common case stores no secret at
all. WebDAV passwords go to the Keychain. Endpoint definitions (name, kind,
host, bucket, region, prefix) live in settings.json; secrets never do.

LICENCE CONSTRAINT: reference-code/cyberduck is GPL-3.0 and this workspace is
MIT with a deny.toml that does not allow GPL. Cyberduck is a BEHAVIOURAL and UX
reference only — its connection-profile concept is worth mirroring, but no code
and no .cyberduckprofile file may be copied. reference-code/rustfs is Apache-2.0
and is the reference for S3 checksum semantics (crates/checksums).

title: ditto --bom gives selective list-driven copy at full fidelity, so sync.rs needs neither rsync nor N processes
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-17. This dissolves the ditto-vs-rsync trade the transfer-crate proposal was built on.

The premise everywhere in this epic was: ditto is the only copier faithful to macOS metadata,
but it copies whole trees, so a SELECTIVE copy (sync's planned subset) needs rsync --files-from,
which costs fidelity — or needs one ditto process per file, which costs 52s where a whole-tree
ditto costs 1.8s (measured, 2000 files).

That premise is false. ditto takes --bom <bomFile>: 'only objects present in index bom are copied'.

Reproduced end to end:
  printf '.\n./a.txt\n./sub\n./sub/c.txt\n' > list.txt
  (cd src && mkbom -s -i list.txt sel.bom)          # /usr/bin/mkbom, ships with macOS
  ditto --bom sel.bom --rsrc --extattr --acl src dst
Result: b.txt correctly NOT copied; a.txt arrived with its xattrs (user.probe,
com.apple.ResourceFork) and its full 8-byte resource fork; ./sub and ./sub/c.txt recreated.

So sync.rs::apply can copy its entire planned set in ONE ditto invocation:
  - full metadata fidelity, same as relocate.rs already relies on
  - no rsync, so no capability probe, and no second authority on 'did the metadata survive'
  - no per-file process spawn, so the 52.38s -> ~1.8s gap closes without any parallelism
  - no new workspace crate, no third-party binary dependency; mkbom and ditto are both
    in /usr/bin on a stock Mac

Gotcha found while verifying: the BOM must contain '.' as its first entry and every parent
directory of every listed path, or mkbom rejects the entry ('Parent . not present in bom')
and ditto copies nothing while exiting 0 — the same silent-empty-success failure shape as
nato-b6h.1, so it needs a post-build assertion that the bom is non-empty.

Next step: replace copy_one()'s per-file ditto loop in sync.rs::apply with a single
bom-driven ditto over the planned entry set.
close_reason: Implemented in 6f7d7d4. sync::apply now copies the planned set in one ditto --bom. Verified at 100,201 entries. This was the finding that decided the council's call.

title: sync_plan/sync_apply are on the IPC surface with no review UI to make them honest
description:
VERIFIED 2026-08-17, raised by the User Advocate seat (council nato-b6h).

src-tauri/src/lib.rs:92-93 now registers commands::sync_plan and commands::sync_apply in
collect_commands!, and src/lib/bindings.ts (+147) and src/lib/ipc.ts (+105) carry the

  - a 'metadata-loss' warning and four others that exist solely to be rendered
None of it renders. A destructive-capable command whose entire safety story is 'the plan
explains it first' is not safe while no plan surface exists.

apply() is also token-gated against a re-plan, which is good, but the token is minted by
plan() — a caller that invokes sync_plan then sync_apply back to back satisfies it without
any human ever seeing a warning.

Either land the review dialog in the same change that exposes the commands, or take the two
lines back out of collect_commands! until it exists. Do not leave it as-is.

title: rgigasync's parallel mode holds the batch mutex across the rsync, so nothing runs in parallel
description: file_processing.rs:77-80 takes the batch_file lock and then runs rsync under it. Every other rayon worker blocks for the whole transfer. The batch_size.store(0) at line 76 is also non-atomic with the swap, so bytes added in between are lost from the count and their files can be sent twice.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-08-17. The second paragraph of this bead's description — that batch_size.store(0)
is non-atomic with the swap and can therefore drop files — is WRONG, and so was a reviewer's
competing claim that peers write into the batch file between run_rsync and the swap.

Settled empirically by the rgigasync-56 session, not by reading: it built the old committed tree
(9084c6c) in a detached worktree, put a RECORDING FAKE rsync on PATH, and counted invocations.
    5 files, all 0 bytes        -> rsync invoked 0 times, exit 0
    same tree + one 1-byte file -> rsync invoked 1 time
No concurrency involved. Both 'lost writes' stories are unreachable:
  - the lock at line 77 is held continuously across run_rsync (79) and the swap (80), so no peer
    can write in that window;
  - a thread that calls store(0) always goes on to lock and rsync the THEN-CURRENT file, so any
    path in the list at the moment of the store is transferred by that same thread, and any path
    written afterwards follows a fetch_add that is also after the store.

The real mechanism is boring and deterministic: current_size only ever grows by metadata.len(),
a zero-byte file adds 0, so the threshold never trips and the final flush is gated on
batch_size > 0 which is still 0. Serial mode has it exactly as badly as parallel.
That is nato-b6h.1, and b6h.1's description was already the correct one. These are ONE bug, not two.

Not exotic, either: any tree under one batch whose files are all empty — lockfiles, __init__.py,
.gitkeep, sentinel files.

mutex across the whole rsync, so every other rayon worker blocks for the duration of the transfer
and 'parallel' mode buys only concurrent metadata() calls. That is a real defect and is unaffected

title: Mature file management: multi-select, bulk actions, and keyboard operation across every list

Nothing supports acting on more than one item at once except the canvas selection feeding the trash drop target, and nothing is reachable from the keyboard. Bulk trash must go through the existing per-item identity revalidation and confirmation token, not a batch shortcut that skips it.

Bands requested: >50 GB, 5 GB, 500 MB, 50 MB, 5 MB, with an implicit remainder below the smallest band. Grouping should re-lay out the treemap against the banded set the same way the category filter does, and the tree table should show the bands as collapsible groups with their own totals and counts.
design: Bands must be decimal SI (50 GB = 50e9) to match the rest of the UI, which docs/05-UI.md pins to 'decimal SI, matching Finder' — mixing a binary 50 GiB band into an SI interface would make the boundary disagree with the size column beside it. The user wrote a mix of Gi and Mb; confirm before shipping if binary is actually wanted. Log-scale size buckets already exist as a planned catalog report (docs/06-DATA.md, Sizes route); this is the live-tree grouping, and the two should share one band definition rather than drift.
acceptance_criteria: A size-band grouping control sits with the existing Colour/Family/Category controls; selecting it groups the table into the named bands with per-band totals and item counts; the treemap re-lays out so band membership is visible; an item appears in exactly one band; the band a file falls into is computed from the same metric the view is set to (logical vs allocated), not silently from one of them.
notes: PARTIALLY DELIVERED in ea4ff7b. Done: the band mechanism itself (binary edges at 5 MiB/50 MiB/500 MiB/5 GiB/50 GiB, chosen to match du -h), the size_bands O(subtree) command over the live arena, and a Sizes route showing every band with BOTH unit renderings on every row (IEC above, SI beneath) plus files, allocated, share and logical. Verified on /Applications: bands sum to 137.7 GB against a 138 GB subtree, 853.6K files. Sizes also left CATALOG_ROUTES since it needs no Parquet partition. STILL OPEN: band grouping as a control inside the Tree route, and treemap re-layout against a banded subset — that half shares its mechanism with nato-4la (category filter), since both need the layout to re-proportion against a filtered set rather than filtering tiles after the batch arrives.

title: Filter the tree and treemap to a category or family, re-laying out to those items only
description: The legend under the chart identifies colours but does nothing when clicked. Selecting a category or family should filter the view to just those entries and re-run the layout against them, so the treemap re-sizes to show the filtered set's own proportions rather than shrinking them inside the unfiltered whole. The tree table below should follow the same filter, and the subtree total should report the filtered bytes. Applies to both the Family and the Category legend rows.
design: The layout command already takes a root and returns tiles for that subtree; a category filter is a second axis and needs a decision on where it applies — filtering candidates inside rdirstat-treemap's gather() keeps one traversal and lets DirTotals stay authoritative, whereas filtering client-side after the Arrow batch arrives cannot re-proportion the tiles. Prefer the former.
acceptance_criteria: Clicking a legend swatch filters chart and table to that category/family; the treemap re-lays out so the filtered items fill the canvas and their relative sizes are readable; the header total reflects the filtered bytes and says it is filtered; the filter clears without a rescan; multi-select across swatches behaves predictably or is explicitly single-select.

title: Relocate: exercise against a real external volume
description: The 19 engine tests all run within one filesystem under target/, so the cross-device path is untested where it matters most. Needs a manual or gated run that: (1) migrates a multi-GB subtree to a genuinely different physical volume and confirms the symlink resolves and the app still reads through it; (2) confirms free space is actually returned on the source volume after emptying the Trash; (3) pulls the destination volume mid-copy and confirms the source survives untouched; (4) confirms ditto carried xattrs and ACLs across an APFS -> exFAT boundary, where it cannot, and that verification therefore FAILS rather than silently dropping metadata. Item 4 is the one most likely to find a real defect: the current verify compares contents, names and symlink targets, but NOT xattrs or ACLs, so an exFAT destination would verify clean while having lost metadata.

title: Relocate: report progress during a multi-gigabyte copy
description: relocate_apply runs ditto and then reads the whole subtree back to verify it. For a 58 GB Docker.raw that is minutes with no feedback beyond a spinner reading 'Copying and verifying…'. The user cannot tell a slow copy from a hung one, and cannot cancel. Needs: a progress event (bytes copied / bytes verified / current path) on the same 10 Hz throttled channel as scan progress, and a cancel that is safe at every step — cancelling during the copy must leave the source untouched and name the partial destination, cancelling after disposal is not offered because there is nothing safe to undo. Blocked on nothing; the engine already has the phase boundaries in the right places.
notes:
VERIFIED 2026-08-17 — the shipped dialog is worse than 'no progress'; it is actively misleading during the flagship case.

src/components/RelocateDialog.tsx:248  confirmLabel = `Moving ${done + 1} of ${actionable.length}…`
  For a single item — the header's own 58 GB Docker.raw case — this string is frozen at
  'Moving 1 of 1…' for the entire multi-hour copy. It counts ITEMS, and the workload is one item.

src/components/RelocateDialog.tsx:339  <Button variant="ghost" onClick={onClose} disabled={running}>
  Cancel is greyed out for the whole operation the user most wants to abort.

src/components/RelocateDialog.tsx:223  if (event.key === 'Escape' && !running) onClose();
  Escape is swallowed while running, so there is no keyboard escape either.

Root cause is not the UI: src-tauri/src/relocate.rs:1119 runs ONE ditto over the whole subtree,
so there is no per-file boundary to report against. Byte-level progress needs either ditto output
parsing or destination stat-polling; a per-file scheduler would emit nothing for a one-file workload.
Council (2026-08-17, nato-b6h) ranked this above any transfer-engine work.
MEASURED 2026-08-17 — ditto -V cannot drive a byte-level progress bar for the flagship case.

  /usr/bin/ditto -V --rsrc --extattr --acl  on a 1 GiB single file:
    [t+0s] >>> Copying /tmp/dbig/a
    [t+0s] copying file ./big.bin ...
    [t+1s] 1073741824 bytes for ./big.bin
  One line when the file starts, one when it finishes. No intra-file progress.

So for a 58 GB Docker.raw, parsing ditto's output yields a single 'copying file ...'
line and then silence for the entire multi-hour copy. Output parsing solves progress
for MANY-file trees only.

The flagship single-huge-file case needs destination stat-polling: poll the
destination path's size (or allocated blocks) on a timer against the known source
size. That works for both shapes, needs no output parsing, and is the smaller change.

Also found: ditto accepts --bom <bomFile>, 'only objects present in index bom are
copied' — so a selective, list-driven batch copy IS possible with ditto, at full
metadata fidelity, without rsync. That dissolves the ditto-vs-rsync trade the
transfer-crate proposal was built on.

title: Publish the tree progressively during a scan instead of only at freeze
description: Today the tree is invisible until the scan finishes ~5 minutes later; the Tree tab is dead the whole time. Publish a new TreeGeneration on a throttled tick during the scan so the tree is browsable while it fills in. The state machine already supports this: state.rs holds RwLock<Option<Arc<CompletedScan>>> with a monotonic TreeGeneration and every read command already rejects stale generations, so the seam exists and no locking change is needed.
design: Copy-on-tick: the builder clones its append-only arena and runs the existing freeze/rollup on the clone, publishing the result through the normal Arc swap. Preserves the frozen-arena contract exactly (no Arc<Mutex<Tree>>, no per-node atomics, per docs/01). Tick interval adapts to tree size so publication cost stays a bounded fraction of scan time.

title: Auto-save the completed scan and auto-load it on launch

Snapshot restores interaction; the Parquet catalog stays a separate projection for reports. Write is temp+fsync+atomic-rename. Load path treats the file as untrusted and goes through Tree::from_parts validation.
acceptance_criteria: App relaunch shows the previous scan's tree without rescanning; load of a ~9M node arena completes in seconds; snapshot is rejected (not crashed on) when the tool version, category hash, or exclusion hash is incompatible; the UI states which scan it loaded and when it was taken.

title: [epic] Relocate: offload a subtree to another volume and leave a symlink
description: Move a heavy subtree (e.g. /private/tmp, a Docker.raw, a Library/Caches tree) off the boot volume onto an external or secondary drive, then leave a symlink at the original path so every existing reference keeps resolving. User decisions (2026-08-17): copy engine is ditto --rsrc --extattr (Apple's own copier — preserves ACLs, xattrs, resource forks and compression that macOS's bundled rsync drops); verification is size + BLAKE3 per file BEFORE the source is unlinked; the pointer left behind is ALWAYS a symlink (firmlinks are reserved for Apple's system volume group and an fstab mount is far more invasive). Two modes: MIGRATE (copy, verify, unlink source, symlink) and REPOINT (the destination already holds the data; just verify and swap in the symlink). Must mirror the existing preview -> token -> re-verify -> apply pattern in src-tauri/src/actions.rs so an action is bound to the generation and selection it was previewed for.
close_reason: Vertical slice delivered and verified live on 2026-08-17. Backend src-tauri/src/relocate.rs: plan -> ditto -> byte-for-byte verify -> symlink pre-flight -> dispose -> symlink, with the same generation-and-(dev,ino)-bound token machinery as Trash, gated behind deletionArmed. Commands relocate_plan/relocate_apply. Frontend RelocateDialog.tsx with volume picker, mode/disposal controls, plan summary and warnings. 25 engine tests. Confirmed on screen: dialog lists mounted volumes with free space, sorts the source's own volume last labelled 'same volume as the source', and refuses an exFAT destination with 'This move cannot proceed' naming the metadata that would be silently lost. Follow-ups tracked separately: progress reporting during long copies, and exercising the cross-device path against a real external volume.

title: Breadcrumbs: build from the ancestor chain, not the click stack
description: useCrumbs in src/components/AppShell.tsx builds the breadcrumb from navStack — the drill-down click stack — so zooming straight to a deep node yields 'RDirStat > / > Docker.raw' and every real ancestor (Users/josh/Library/Containers/com.docker.docker/Data/vms/0/data) is unreachable. (2) Every APFS volume in a container shows identical capacity/used/free, because df reports container-wide totals and the UI derives used = total - available; the per-volume Used column df already prints is parsed and thrown away. (3) Volumes are listed flat, so there is no way to see that Macintosh HD, VM, Preboot, Update and Data are one APFS container on one physical disk.

Verified on screen: one 'APPLE SSD AP1024Z 1.00 TB INTERNAL - 3 containers' group replacing three duplicate disk headers, per-volume used (Data 928 GB) instead of four identical '968 GB used' rows, and the list scrolls.

Publish per-class counts live and expose the retained detail list through a command so both the live strip and the completion alert can answer 'what are these errors'.

title: offload-to-external.sh manifest_of claims NUL-safety it does not have
description:
Found by the Skeptic seat on the nato-b6h verification council, 2026-08-18.

scripts/offload-to-external.sh manifest_of walks its input NUL-delimited (find -print0 |
sort -z | read -d '') but EMITS newline-delimited records with printf '...\n'. So a filename
containing a newline splits one record into two, and 'ls -lde | sed -n 2,$p' then reads the
tail of the filename as the ACL field.

The OUTCOME is currently safe: both sides corrupt identically, so the source and destination
manifests still compare equal for a faithful copy and still differ for a lossy one. The defect
is that the header comment claims NUL-safety the emitter does not provide, and a future reader
will rely on it.

Fix: emit NUL-delimited records too, and compare with cmp on the raw streams rather than with
diff on lines. Low priority precisely because the outcome is sound today — but the comment
must not outlive the property.

title: relocate verifies extended attributes but not ACLs
description:
4fe457a added verify_extended_attributes, closing council condition C1 for xattrs (which
includes resource forks, carried as com.apple.ResourceFork). ACLs are still not compared.

Why it was scoped out rather than forgotten:
  - acl_get_file(3) needs unsafe extern FFI, which this crate may not have — the workspace
    denies unsafe_code outside rdirstat-scan::sys::bulk (see the crate::volumes header for
    the same call being made for statfs).
  - The shell-out equivalent is 'ls -lRe', whose ACL lines are interleaved with the long
    listing and would need fragile parsing, unlike 'xattr -r' which is one clean line per
    (path, attribute).
  - Measured priority: in the fidelity matrix (nato-b6h.7) every copier that lost ACLs also
    lost xattrs, and no copier lost ACLs while keeping xattrs. So the xattr check is a proxy
    that catches every loss observed so far. It is a proxy, not a proof, which is why this
    is filed rather than assumed.

Do this when either: a crate is permitted to own an ACL binding, or a copy is observed that
kept extended attributes and dropped an ACL — which would falsify the proxy above.

title: AionUi is a 1.1 GB uncited reference checkout — justify it or delete it
description:
reference-code/AGENTS.md now carries a row for AionUi/ (Electron 37 + React 19 desktop GUI for CLI AI agents, Apache-2.0, tag v2.1.55, 1.1 GB — the largest checkout in the folder). Nothing tracked cites it: 'git grep AionUi -- docs skills src src-tauri crates' returns nothing.

reference-code/AGENTS.md's own rule is that a checkout with no citation is a question mark, so this is filed rather than left implicit. Two acceptable outcomes:

1. Write the reason it is here into the doc that will use it (docs/05-UI.md is the only plausible home), and add the citation to the index row.
2. Delete the clone and flip the row to 'Status: absent', keeping the prose — the index rule is that a row is never deleted when a clone goes missing.

Extra weight on option 2: AionUi ships a full competing agent harness (.claude/skills for architecture/bump-version/i18n/testing, .claude/commands/, .gemini/, .specify/, a 154-line AGENTS.md instructing agents to follow its own architecture skill and a <=10-children-per-directory rule). It is recorded in the hazard table in reference-code/AGENTS.md, but the cheapest way to remove the hazard is to remove the clone.

title: Sync: report progress and allow cancel during a large copy
description:
Sync folders is verified end-to-end on a 3-file fixture (plan: 2 to copy / 1 already there / nothing removed; apply: 26 B written, destination-only file untouched). It has no progress and no cancel, which only shows up at real sizes.

Two distinct silences:

1. The PLAN walk. walk() takes an explicit cap — 5000 entries for display, usize::MAX for apply. On a large source the Check button sits there with no feedback while the walk runs, and the user cannot tell a slow walk from a hung one.
2. The APPLY copy. Since the peer's one-ditto refactor the whole planned set goes to a single ditto invocation, so there is exactly one long-running child process and no per-file callback to hang a counter on.

Cancel is the sharper half: there is currently no way to stop a sync once started. ditto is a child process, so cancellation means killing it — which leaves a partially-copied tree. That is safe by construction (sync only ever ADDS files, never removes or overwrites unless asked) but the UI has to say so rather than imply a clean rollback.

Shares a mechanism with nato-6zb (relocate progress) — both need a copy-progress channel from a ditto child up to the frontend. Worth solving once for both rather than twice.
acceptance_criteria: A sync of a tree large enough to take >2s shows live progress for both the plan walk and the copy, and can be cancelled; after a cancel the UI states plainly that files already copied were kept and nothing was removed.

title: Sync, storage and move destinations need a folder chooser, not a typed path
description: All three path fields were bare text inputs, which asks the user to have memorised a path. It is also not equivalent: docs/03-MACOS.md names NSOpenPanel as the explicit-consent path for folders, so a picked directory is one macOS has authorised this process to read while the same characters typed carry no grant. Adds tauri-plugin-dialog with only dialog:allow-open granted, a pickFolder() wrapper at the ipc.ts boundary, and a shared PathField used by SyncRoute, StoragePanel and RelocateDialog.
acceptance_criteria: Browse opens at the field's current value; cancelling changes nothing; typing still works for pasted paths and not-yet-created folders.

title: scripts/offload-to-external.sh: relocate large fixed data off the internal drive
description:
Docker Desktop is already moved. Remaining internal-drive bulk that is relocatable: kaspad mainnet data (13 GB), npm _cacache (24 GB), pnpm cache-dir (7.5 GB). Needs a reversible, verified migration to /Volumes/tuf8tb.

Constraint discovered during investigation: the pnpm STORE must not be relocated. ~/Library/pnpm/store/v10 (7.4 GB) is hardlinked into live node_modules under ~/huyang-apps, ~/dyad-apps and ~/lobot-apps. pnpm keeps one store per volume precisely so hardlinks work; moving it to the external drive would make pnpm fall back to copying and consume MORE space overall. The store gets pruned, not moved. Only cache-dir moves.
acceptance_criteria: Dry-run default. Every move is rsync-verified before the source is deleted. --revert restores the original layout. Refuses to move the pnpm store and says why. Checks destination volume is mounted and has room. Refuses to migrate a service that is currently running.
close_reason: Committed as 7895938 + this fix. kaspad's 12.8 GB moved and symlinked (verified readable, kaspad.conf left in place); npm and pnpm caches discarded and repointed at /Volumes/tuf8tb/.offload via --fresh (verified: ~/.npmrc and ~/Library/Preferences/pnpm/rc both updated, a real 'pnpm add' wrote to the new location). pnpm store correctly refused relocation and was pruned instead.

title: Escalate before you spend: price a lookup after cache, known-good sets, and signature
description: The rule that makes 500 lookups/day workable, spanning phase 9 and 10 (docs/10-TRUST.md, 'Local checks are what make 500 lookups a day workable'). reputation_plan resolves a selection in order — cache hit, known-good hash-set match, Apple-signed/notarized signature — and only prices what is left. The preflight reads '40 lookups: 260 of your 300 selected files were answered locally', breakdown expandable. Signature-based skipping is user-disableable, and 'look it up anyway' remains one click in the details panel.
acceptance_criteria: A 300-file selection of mostly signed or known-good software prices well under 300 lookups and shows why; overriding for a single file still works.

title: Assurance ladder, badge, and the right-click / selection-bar verbs
description: Steps 3 and 6 of docs/07-BUILD-PHASES.md#phase-9-local-assurance, and the interaction the user asked for. The ordered Assurance enum plus the Findings list, the derived badge with published worst-first precedence, and a sortable/filterable table column. Every badge expands into its evidence with dates. Verbs land in the existing row context menu (TreeTable/DataTable/canvas) and the SelectionActions bar: local verbs are unmetered with no preflight and stay enabled with no key; the metered verb carries its cost and remaining daily allowance inline in the menu item. Nothing runs unless invoked.
acceptance_criteria: 'No assurance' is neutral styling, not a warning — it is what almost every document will be; no check runs without a user action; local verbs work with no key configured.

title: XProtect rules via yara-x, plus magic-byte-vs-extension mismatch
description: Step 5 of docs/07-BUILD-PHASES.md#phase-9-local-assurance. Evaluate the running system's XProtect.bundle YARA rules in-process via yara-x (BSD-3-Clause, already in deny.toml's allow list). Rules are read from the live system, never copied, cached beyond a session, or redistributed. The bundle path and format are Apple's unversioned internal detail, so absence or a compile failure reports XProtectUnavailable. Separately: compare magic bytes against the claimed extension over the classifier's existing head read, bounded to 4 KiB, as a Finding rather than a verdict.
acceptance_criteria: Matched-no-rule never renders as clean; a missing or malformed bundle reports unavailable; a synthetic rule set exercises both match and no-match paths.

title: Code signature and notarization via Security.framework, in one quarantined FFI module
description: Step 2 of docs/07-BUILD-PHASES.md#phase-9-local-assurance. SecStaticCodeCreateWithPath / SecStaticCodeCheckValidity / SecCodeCopySigningInformation for Team ID, authority chain, cdhash, flags. No codesign/spctl subprocess per file. Verification reads every code page, so it is on-demand only, never during a scan; deep nested verification is a separate opt-in mode. Open question for this issue: whether an unstapled notarization ticket can be checked offline — if not, the online check is a setting off by default and the ladder says 'notarization not established'.
acceptance_criteria: unsafe confined to one module per docs/08-RUST-PRACTICES.md; a signed bundle with one modified resource reports SignatureBroken; verifying a 4 GB bundle is cancellable.

title: Imported hash sets: load digests against files, exact membership, user-declared polarity
description: Step 4 of docs/07-BUILD-PHASES.md#phase-9-local-assurance, and the 'load hashes in general' capability. Accepts a plain digest list (algorithm inferred from hex length), CSV with a named column, and the NSRL RDSv3 modern-minimal SHA-256 publication. Polarity (known-good vs known-bad) is chosen by the user at import and NEVER inferred — guessing is how an IOC feed becomes an allowlist. Import rewrites to an app-owned sorted mmapped digest structure: exact answers, O(log n), page-cache resident. A probabilistic filter is the documented fallback only if disk cost is rejected, and its matches must render as probable. One read computes every digest a loaded set needs.
acceptance_criteria: Disk cost projected before import starts; malformed lines reported by line number, never silently skipped; every match names its set and import date; removing a set removes its findings.

title: Phase 9 — local assurance: the trust ladder without a third party
description: Plan is docs/10-TRUST.md. No network, no key, no quota — works offline for a user who never enables VirusTotal. Code signature + notarization via Security.framework, XProtect rules via yara-x, quarantine/WhereFroms provenance, magic-byte-vs-extension mismatch, and imported hash sets. Produces the Assurance ladder + Findings list + derived badge.
design: No numeric score: an ordered enum (AppleSystem > NotarizedDeveloper > SignedDeveloper > AdHocSigned > Unsigned > NotApplicable > Unchecked) plus a Findings list, with a published worst-first badge precedence. A number would have to assign a value to 'no evidence', which is the majority state, and every value misleads. The enum still sorts, filters and groups.
acceptance_criteria: With no key ever configured every check answers; a signed bundle with a modified resource reports SignatureBroken; a missing XProtect bundle reports unavailable, never clean; empty results render as 'found nothing', never as safe.

title: scripts/reclaim-space.sh: re-runnable disk reclaim with Rust-aware target sweeping
description: The dev machine sits at 85% full (756/926 GB). Package-manager caches, dormant container VMs, and Rust build artifacts account for ~200 GB. Rust is the dominant repeat cost: this repo alone holds 47 GB in target/ (9.5 GB incremental, 18.7 GB in stale per-agent CARGO_TARGET_DIRs) plus 9.4 GB in src-tauri/target. Need one idempotent script, dry-run by default, that reclaims caches without forcing a full cold rebuild of whatever is being actively worked on.
acceptance_criteria: Dry-run is the default; --apply required to delete. Groups are selectable. Rust sweeping is age-aware and has a cheap 'incremental only' level that does not destroy dependency artifacts. Never removes the active/default rustup toolchain. Never rm -rf's the pnpm store out from under existing node_modules hardlinks. Re-runnable with no errors when targets are already gone.
close_reason: scripts/reclaim-space.sh committed as ce505f1. Dry-run default, group selection, three Rust levels, pnpm-store and cargo-index footguns encoded. Verified: apply path on a fixture (deps survive incremental sweep), idempotent re-run, safety guard, empty-roots under set -u.

title: One context-menu root per row instead of one per table
description:
src/components/SizeBands.tsx was mounting a Radix ContextMenu root per row — up to 250 portals — which nato-rdirstat-ee's agent found and fixed. DataTable.tsx's own header docblock states the rule it was violating.

src/components/TreeTable.tsx repeats the pattern: a context-menu root per row, at up to 500 rows per page. NOT measured, so the cost is unquantified — but it is the same shape as the case already found and fixed, and the rule is stated in the file it sits next to.

FIX: one root for the table, positioned at the pointer, reading the row under the cursor at open time rather than binding a root per row.

Measure before and after rather than assuming. If the cost turns out to be negligible at 500 rows, close this with the number rather than leaving the question open — an unmeasured performance issue that nobody can close is its own kind of debt.

title: The JavaScript test suite is not in the project quality gate
description: 'just check' runs check-docs, fmt, lint (clippy + tsc), the Rust tests, and a frontend build — but nothing runs the 10 JavaScript test files. They pass (107 tests via 'node --test $(find src -name "*.test.ts")'), so this is an enforcement gap rather than a rot problem, but an unenforced guard rots on its own schedule. src/lib/categories.test.ts is the one that matters most: categories.ts documents it as the thing keeping the TypeScript category list in step with rdirstat-classify/src/defaults.rs, and a category-id drift is exactly what it exists to catch.
design: Do NOT add vitest. Every existing test file uses node:test with node:assert/strict and Node's built-in TypeScript stripping, and format.test.ts's header documents that choice explicitly. Two runners in one repo is a decision to make deliberately, not to arrive at because someone reached for the familiar tool — an agent did exactly that today, ran 'npx vitest', found it missing, and concluded the tests do not run at all.
acceptance_criteria: 'just check' fails when a JavaScript test fails; the command used is the documented 'node --test' convention rather than a newly added runner dependency; package.json gains a 'test' script so the invocation is discoverable rather than folklore.

title: Cache filtered layout weights so resizing a filtered view is not 163 ms per frame
description: A filtered layout costs one extra O(subtree) pass. Measured on the 12.27M-node boot volume: 0.35 ms unfiltered against 163.12 ms filtered. That is fine for toggling a filter, where the dim gives instant feedback while the real layout runs, and it is not fine per resize step — dragging a window edge with a filter active re-runs the whole pass on every layout request. The weights depend on (generation, root, metric, category set) and NOT on the viewport, so a resize can reuse them entirely.
design: Cache lives in src-tauri rather than rdirstat-treemap: the crate is stateless by design and layout_tiles is a pure function of its inputs, which is what makes it testable and deterministic. A small memo in AppState keyed by (generation, root, metric, set-digest) holding the last FilteredWeights would do it; a one-entry cache is probably enough, since the user filters one view at a time.
acceptance_criteria: Resizing a filtered view does not recompute FilteredWeights; a filter change or a root change does; the cache is dropped when the generation changes, like every other generation-keyed state; the measured resize cost with a filter active approaches the unfiltered figure.
close_reason: Landed. AppState memoises the last FilteredWeights keyed by (generation, root, metric, set), and layout_tiles_with reuses them. Measured: 163.12 ms per filtered request before, 0.14-0.19 ms across two window resizes after. One entry rather than a map, since each is ~10 MB at 1.2M directories and the user filters one view at a time. Also fixed the instrument: the cache moved the cost out of layout_tiles' timer, so the weights build is now timed where it actually happens.

title: Interactive verification is single-occupant: debug builds cannot serve dist/, and cargo run touches bindings.ts
description:
Two related constraints found while verifying the category filter with three sessions live in one checkout. Both cost real time to rediscover.

1. A DEBUG BUILD CANNOT BE POINTED AT dist/. src-tauri/Cargo.toml defines no custom-protocol feature, so a debug 'cargo run' always loads from tauri.conf.json's devUrl (http://localhost:1420). There is no cheap way to run against a static bundle; the only options are exclusive use of the vite dev server or a full 'cargo tauri build --debug'. Consequence: only ONE session can meaningfully verify interactively at a time, because HMR from any other session's src/ edit remounts the app and resets every useState. This is invisible in production and looks exactly like 'the feature does not work' — during this session a legend flipped Family->Category->Family on its own, which no click can do.

2. EVERY 'cargo run' REWRITES src/lib/bindings.ts. src-tauri/src/lib.rs's run() calls export_bindings("../src/lib/bindings.ts") under #[cfg(debug_assertions)] on every start. Verified: bindings.ts mtime moved to 18:05:57, exactly the launch of a cargo run, with byte-identical content (git reported the file clean). Vite watches that path, so restarting the app remounts the frontend independently of any other session. A verification loop that involves restarting the app is therefore remounting itself.

Found by nato-rdirstat-ee (point 2) and nato-rdirstat-58 (point 1); mtime confirmed rather than assumed.

Possible fixes, none chosen: add a custom-protocol feature so a debug build can serve dist/; make export_bindings write only when the content differs; or gate it behind an env var so a verification run can opt out.
notes: Confirmed again 2026-08-18 while verifying the sync tab, plus four new failure modes now captured in memory key rdirstat-gui-verification-on-a-shared-mac: same-named peer processes make every AppleScript process specifier ambiguous (whose-unix-id returns the WRONG pid), the window teleports so clicks must be window-relative, the first click after frontmost is swallowed, and cliclick drops the cmd modifier under load. Also observed: a peer's cliclick landed inside my app instance and started a full 8 TB scan twice, and the webview went permanently blank while vite still served 200 and tsc was clean (only a process restart recovered it).

title: Show a size-band entry in the tree, so a found file can be explored in context
description: The size-band breakdown identifies a file by full path but offers no way to jump to it in the tree, so after finding the largest file on the disk the user has to navigate to it by hand. Add a 'Show in tree' action that sets the navigation stack to the file's ancestor chain and selects it, the same way the breadcrumb navigation already sets an exact root-to-node path.
acceptance_criteria: Invoking the action from a band entry switches to the Tree route, expands to the file's parent, selects the file, and scrolls it into view; the navigation stack matches the ancestor chain so the breadcrumb and the up-one-level button both behave; a file whose ancestors cannot be resolved reports that rather than navigating somewhere arbitrary.

title: Verify the scan-error popover on screen during a live scan
description: The scan_errors path is verified end to end in Rust (engine test: a refused directory shows up in the live per-class counters and the sample list with its path), and the UI wiring typechecks, but the status strip's error popover and the completion-alert disclosure have not been seen rendering against a real scan — the shared checkout's build was mid-refactor by other sessions during the verification window. Start a scan of a permission-dense root (e.g. ~/Library or /), click the 'N unreadable' counter in the status strip, and confirm the class breakdown and sample paths render and refresh at 1 Hz; then let it finish and confirm 'Show the failed paths' under the completion alerts shows the same list.
acceptance_criteria: Screenshot of the live popover during a scan and of the completion disclosure afterwards.
close_reason: Verified: during a live scan of /Volumes/tuf8tb the strip showed '2 unreadable' as a button, and opening it rendered 'Recorded failures' with the class breakdown (macOS refused access, 2), the Full-Disk-Access guidance, and both sample paths with operation and errno (/Volumes/tuf8tb/.DocumentRevisions-V100-bad-1 and /.Trashes, opening a folder, errno 13/1).

title: Add a settings/configuration entry point to the main window and the tray panel
description: There is no way to reach settings from either GUI. The Titlebar component already accepts an onOpenSettings prop and renders a gear when given one, but AppShell never passes it, so the gear is not rendered. The tray panel header carries only a refresh control. Wire up a settings entry point in both surfaces and give it something to open: scan options (exclusions, cross-filesystem, hard-link policy, aggregation), snapshot retention and on-disk sizes, and the deletion-arming preference that currently lives loose in the details panel.
acceptance_criteria: A configuration control is reachable from the main window titlebar and from the tray panel; it opens a settings surface rather than a dead icon; keyboard focus and VoiceOver reach it; the control is visually consistent between the two surfaces.

title: Add a Cleanup tab that surfaces common reclaim paths with what is safe to remove
description: The existing tabs (Tree, Types, Sizes, Ages, Diff, Dupes) all answer 'what is on disk'. None answers 'what should I do about it', which is the actual user goal on a volume at 97.3 percent full with 27.2 GB free. Add a tab that ranks recognised, well-understood reclaim targets by recoverable bytes and says plainly what each one is and what removing it costs: build and dependency caches, package manager caches, developer tool derived data, browser and app caches, device backups, container images, downloads and installers, large old files, and the Trash. Each entry explains what regenerates automatically versus what is gone for good.
design: Build on rdirstat-classify context tags rather than a second path-matching engine, so the taxonomy stays in one place. Recovery figures are reported as logical bytes with an honest range on APFS, never as a guaranteed physical reclaim, consistent with the duplicate-detection language in docs/06-DATA.md.
acceptance_criteria: Tab lists reclaim candidates ranked by recovered bytes with a plain-English description of consequence per candidate; every candidate resolves to real paths from the current scan, never a hardcoded guess that may not exist; nothing is removed without the existing armed-deletion plus confirmation-token path; candidates whose contents regenerate are visually distinct from candidates that are permanent loss.

title: Rescan one subtree and splice it into the loaded tree
description: After a snapshot reload the tree can be stale in one place the user just changed. Re-walking the whole volume costs ~5 minutes to refresh one folder. Add a subtree rescan: select a directory, re-walk only it, and splice the result into the existing arena, re-rolling its ancestor chain. Exact and deterministic, needs no Full Disk Access and no FSEvents event-store handling.
design: Chosen over mtime-gated whole-tree delta because on APFS writing into an existing file does not touch the parent directory mtime, so mtime gating silently misses in-place file growth. FSEvents since-last-scan remains the eventual automatic path; the snapshot manifest should carry the event ID from the start so that stays additive.
acceptance_criteria: Rescanning a subtree updates that subtree and every ancestor total without touching unrelated nodes; a subtree rescan of a small folder completes in about a second; the spliced tree passes the same structural validation as a freshly frozen one; the UI shows which subtree was refreshed and when.

title: Show scan progress as % of volume covered, with a red→orange→yellow→green ramp
description: Progress today is a raw pending-dir count ('160.6K pending'), which gives no sense of how far along the scan is. Both numbers needed for a real denominator already exist: allocated-bytes-observed and the volume's used bytes. The screenshot shows 869 GB observed of 967 GB used = ~90%. Surface that as a percentage plus a colour ramp that walks red -> orange -> yellow -> green as coverage rises, in the status bar and the menu-bar tray.
acceptance_criteria: Status bar shows a coverage percentage derived from observed allocated bytes over volume used bytes; the ramp advances red -> orange -> yellow -> green with coverage; the number is presented as an estimate, never as a completion guarantee, since unreadable and excluded paths make observed bytes a floor.
close_reason: Landed in 1c277cb + 54b7669. Scan panel now shows a coverage bar with a large percentage and a red->orange->yellow->green ramp on its own four tokens (not the capacity-pressure ones, which mean 'disk nearly full' on the same screen). Denominator is volume used_bytes for a whole-volume scan and directories-known for a subtree, labelled either way; percentage floored and capped at 99 while running. Verified on screen at 72% (yellow) and 80% (green).

title: Add a categories() command so the UI stops mirroring the Rust table by hand
description: src/lib/categories.ts hand-mirrors the id->key->label table compiled in crates/rdirstat-classify/src/defaults.rs. Nothing at runtime reconciles them: Rust sends a bare u8. The two silently diverged once already — the compiled table grew ids 19..24 (package, media-library, build-junk, cache, font, database) and the frontend stopped at 18, so node_modules and DerivedData painted as an unlabelled --cat-unknown grey. categories.test.ts now parses defaults.rs and asserts key-for-key equality, which catches the drift, but the mechanism that produces it is still there. Real fix: a categories() Tauri command returning the compiled table (id, key, label, rgb) plus its ConfigHash, with the static table demoted to a boot-time fallback. Raised by nato-rdirstat-38 during the colour-coding fix.

title: Menu-bar tray icon with a passive mini panel
description: Add a macOS menu-bar presence so the app can be kept an eye on without the main window: a template tray icon, a right-click menu (Open, Rescan, Quit), and a left-click mini panel window showing volume pressure per physical disk and the last completed scan's totals. The panel is read-only and refreshes on a slow timer; catalog (Parquet/DuckDB) statistics slot into it when phase 6 lands. Closing the main window leaves the app running in the menu bar.
acceptance_criteria: Tray icon appears; left click opens a positioned panel window; menu opens the main window and quits; closing the main window does not quit; panel refreshes volumes passively.
notes: Landed: src-tauri/src/tray.rs (template icon, menu Open/Show Status Panel/Quit, left-click panel window, focus-loss hide, close-hides-main-window), TrayPanel.tsx (disks by container, last scan, catalog-not-in-this-build note, Open button), App.tsx routes on ?window=tray. Verified on screen: icon renders, menu opens, panel window shows. Found and fixed: panel positioned in physical pixels walked across displays (1394 -> 2788 -> 4250 points); now logical points with clamp_to_monitor + tests.
close_reason: Landed and verified live on screen at commit c519b30: deletion arming (switch off by default, inert drop target), the status strip's 'N unreadable' popover showing per-class counts and sample paths during a running scan, the volume picker scrolling and grouped by physical disk with per-volume used bytes, and the menu-bar tray icon, menu and status panel.

title: Handle terminal reality: colour depth, width, unicode, resize, non-TTY
description: Truecolor/256/16/no-colour with NO_COLOR honoured, ordered column dropping as width shrinks, --ascii, escaped non-UTF-8 names, SIGWINCH relayout without rescan or lost selection, and a usage error rather than escape codes when stdout is not a TTY. docs/09-TUI.md#terminal-reality

description: Category totals for the selected subtree come from the phase-2 arena walk. Percentiles, histograms, and age tables wait for the closed report enum in phase 7 and say so in the UI. Writing a Rust histogram to fill the gap creates the second statistics implementation that 05 and 06 both exist to prevent. docs/09-TUI.md#reports-are-the-same-closed-enum-rendered-as-text

Configure Developer ID signing, hardened runtime, notarization, and stapling before permission-flow acceptance
Implement reactive privacy/FDA guidance from actual operation/path errors — no invented global FDA boolean
Complete package presentation, firmlink defense, volume capability/capacity reporting, snapshot presence, scan-vs-volume explanations
Record scanner, WebView, and total desktop process-group RSS separately; set the desktop release ceiling without weakening the phase-1 scanner ceiling

title: relocate migration test asserts Ordinary risk, so it fails when run from /private/tmp
description: relocate::tests::a_migration_copies_verifies_removes_the_source_and_leaves_a_symlink asserts plan.risk == RiskTier::Ordinary, but assess_risk classifies /private/tmp as Risky (asserted deliberately at relocate.rs:1304). The test builds its fixture in a temp dir, so it passes on a checkout under /Volumes and fails on one under /tmp — found while verifying unrelated work in a detached worktree at /tmp/mw. The fixture should be rooted somewhere the risk assessor calls ordinary, the way storage::tests::scratch() already does with target/storage-scratch.
acceptance_criteria: The test passes regardless of where the checkout lives.

title: Changing the snapshot folder should offer to move what is already stored
description: set_snapshot_dir deliberately does not move existing snapshots — moving gigabytes as a side effect of editing a preference is not something a settings control should do silently, and the store is a rebuildable cache. But leaving the old files behind means the user pays for them twice until they notice. Offer an explicit 'move N snapshots (X GB) to the new folder' step after a successful change, reusing the relocate module's ditto-copy-verify-then-remove protocol rather than a second implementation.
acceptance_criteria: The offer states the count and byte size; a failed or cancelled move leaves both copies intact; the source is only removed after verification.

title: Tier 2: single-file sample upload behind a per-digest consent token
description: Step 5 of docs/10-REPUTATION.md, last and GUI-only. POST /files for <=32MB, /files/upload_url for 32-650MB, >650MB refused locally with the limit stated. Egress::Sample cannot be constructed without a SampleConsent minted by the dialog and naming its digest. Dialog quotes the vendor's sharing term verbatim, shows the exact filename to be transmitted and lets the user replace it. fstat re-checked before the body is read. Analysis polling on bounded backoff (15/30/60/120/240s) drawn from the same ledger. POST is never auto-retried.
acceptance_criteria: No code path constructs Egress::Sample without a token; a consent for digest A cannot be spent on digest B; a file changed between hash and send aborts with FileChanged and is never sent; no batch upload path exists.

title: Quota ledger and the meter, built before the first lookup ships
description: Step 3 of docs/10-REPUTATION.md, and the capability the user explicitly asked for: see the daily allowance against actual use, before spending it. Free tier is 4/min, 500/day, 15.5K/month. Reserve before send, commit on completion, refund only what never left the process; a 429 is not refunded. Windows roll forward only so a backwards clock jump under-spends. Ledger keyed by a digest of the key. Reconcile against overall_quotas at most every 15 min, never during a batch — the meter must not exhaust the quota. Optional daily reserve (default 50) that batches cannot consume.
acceptance_criteria: Meter shows minute/day/month used-vs-allowed with reset times and says which numbers are the vendor's; a batch states its cost against what remains and its projected finish under the 4/min ceiling before it starts; property tests show no window is ever exceeded under concurrency or clock jumps.

title: Tier 1: digest lookups, verdict cache, and file-provenance URL/domain/IP reports
description: Step 4 of docs/10-REPUTATION.md. GET /files/{sha256} over the phase-8 hashing protocol (fstat before/after, no symlink follow). Verdict cache keyed by digest, storing the vendor's last_analysis_date and our fetched-at; no view renders a verdict without its age. Provenance from com.apple.metadata:kMDItemWhereFroms and com.apple.quarantine feeds /urls, /domains, /ip_addresses — the extracted URL is shown in full before it is sent.
acceptance_criteria: 404 renders as 'not known to VirusTotal' and never as clean or green; files with no provenance xattrs offer no lookup and make no request; fake-server suite covers every parsed response and error variant with no live traffic in just check.

title: Keychain custody for the VirusTotal API key, with redaction tests
description: Step 2 of docs/10-REPUTATION.md. Store the user-supplied key as a Keychain generic password under the bundle id — never Application Support, never a snapshot. Frontend sees only ReputationConfig{configured,hint,tier}. Hand-written Debug prints ApiKey(****).
acceptance_criteria: Tests assert no Debug/Display/error/log path emits any substring of the key; clearing the key offers, as a separate decision, to clear the verdict cache.

title: rdirstat-reputation crate + settle the reqwest/rustls licence and dependency cost
description: Step 1 of docs/10-REPUTATION.md. New crate crates/rdirstat-reputation with reqwest (default-features=false, rustls-tls/json/multipart/stream). Scan path and the webview-free CLI bin must still link no HTTP/TLS stack; CLI gets a 'reputation' feature off by default. deny.toml's licenses.allow does not currently admit ring's expression — pick a backend it admits or record a justified exceptions entry. Also verify whether GET /users/{id}/overall_quotas answers a free key; docs/10 marks that unverified.
acceptance_criteria: just audit is green; cargo tree shows no reqwest/rustls under rdirstat-core/scan/classify; the overall_quotas answer is recorded in docs/10-REPUTATION.md.

title: Phase 10 — optional VirusTotal reputation lookups
description: Plan is docs/10-TRUST.md. Optional, off by default, user-supplied API key, first network egress in the product. Three egress tiers: nothing / digest / sample. Depends on the phase-9 local assurance layer, which resolves most files before a lookup is ever priced. Steps in docs/07-BUILD-PHASES.md#phase-10-reputation-lookups-optional.
design: Naming discipline: never 'virus scanner', never 'clean', 404 = 'not known to VirusTotal'. No bundled key. Key in Keychain, never crosses IPC toward the webview. All HTTP Rust-side; CSP not loosened.
acceptance_criteria: With the feature off the binary makes zero network calls and no scan behaviour changes.

title: 336 MB of cargo build output is sitting inside crates/rdirstat-core/src/
description: crates/rdirstat-core/src/target/ holds 336 MB of build artefacts — someone ran cargo with CARGO_TARGET_DIR pointed inside the source tree. It is gitignored so nothing is committed, but every repo-wide grep or rg returns binary .rlib/.rmeta hits from it, which is a real drag on anyone searching the codebase. Not deleted yet: several sessions and agents are building concurrently and one of them may have that directory as its active target, so removing it mid-build would break someone's compile.
acceptance_criteria: The directory is gone; no session is mid-build against it when it is removed; a repo-wide grep returns no binary hits from inside crates/.
